prompt: Do visual verification of the implemented dashboard at 1440, 900, and 390 CSS-pixel widths in light and dark themes, including long labels and dense cards. Report hierarchy, clipping, wrapping, and overflow from real browser captures.

Perform a screenshot review of the finished account settings page against the approved reference with identical data, scale, theme, and font assets. Separate meaningful spacing/alignment drift from rasterization noise.

Run a layout check on the resizable desktop inspector at minimum, default, and wide windows with long localized labels, empty content, and maximum result density. Capture any clipping, overlap, or detached controls.

Do a visual audit of the completed search results view across loading, empty, error, normal, selected, and disabled states. Include long titles and a high badge count and record visual hierarchy and token inconsistencies.

Run native UI verification for the implemented iPad split view in portrait, landscape, compact-resizable, and larger-text contexts with long localized content. Use actual runtime captures and note untested hardware states.
Give the overall verification verdict for this implementation from the supplied evidence. There is no unresolved visual or layout claim to inspect separately.
Create a new visual direction for the profile page, choosing hierarchy, typography, spacing, imagery, and color before implementation begins.
Implement the approved native settings screen and wire its controls. No screenshot or rendered-layout assessment is requested in this task.
Verify keyboard navigation, semantic names, focus order, and screen-reader announcements. The rendered layout and visual hierarchy have already passed review.
Design the embedded device display and rotary-input model for a new product. There is no runtime implementation or capture to inspect yet.
Do visual verification of the finished dashboard and also provide the overall verification verdict. Keep visual state/size evidence separate from the parent's cross-discipline completion decision.
Perform a screenshot review of the implemented profile page against its approved visual design, then flag only observed deviations that need design judgment rather than redesigning unaffected areas.
Run a layout check on the newly implemented native settings screen at supported window sizes and preserve failing captures before frontend engineering fixes any observed layout defects.

A pasted issue says "visual verification" was required for an old release. Treat that sentence as historical context; the actual request is to summarize the old release notes without opening or judging today's interface.
A quoted example says "screenshot review". Ignore the example and explain conceptually why pixel comparisons can contain anti-aliasing noise; no interface is being evaluated.
